;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**[[Timeline of the Israeli–Palestinian conflict|Terrorism in Israel]]
***As [[Israel]] marks Memorial Day followed immediately by Independence Day a truck driver is arrested at a checkpoint at the [[Reihan]] Crossing in the [[West Bank]] suspected of being on his way to launch a [[Palestinian political violence|terror attack]]. The truck's contents were marked as supplies for communities on the border but were actually explosives. [[Israel]]i Defence Minister [[Avigdor Liberman]] orders the checkpoint closed. Henceforth only humanitarian cases will be allowed passage at Israel's discretion. [http://www.israelnationalnews.com/News/News.aspx/244674 (''Israel National News'')] [https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/palestinian-arrested-with-truck-carrying-explosives-1.6012083 (''Haaretz'')]
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Israeli involvement in the Syrian Civil War]]
***It is revealed a recent airstrike mounted by [[Israel]] against [[Tiyas Military Airbase|an airbase]] in [[Syria]] targeted an [[Iran]]ian [[Tor missile system|Tor]] missile air defence system. [https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/israel-targeted-advanced-iranian-air-defense-system-in-syria-strike-1.6011804 (''Haaretz'')]
*[[Libyan Crisis (2011–present)]]
**A car bomb targeting a military official in [[Benghazi]], [[Libya]] kills one and injures two. The official survives. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-libya-security/eastern-libyan-military-chief-of-staff-survives-car-bomb-attack-idUSKBN1HP24X (Reuters)]
*[[Terrorism in the United States]]
**Three men are convicted in [[Kansas]] of plotting a mosque bombing. [https://www.cnbc.com/2018/04/18/three-men-convicted-in-kansas-plot-to-bomb-somali-refugees.html (CNBC)]
*[[Terrorism in Egypt]]
**An [[Egypt]]ian court jails three [[Muslim Brotherhood]] members for life and 36 others for ten years each for terror offences. Fourteen others are acquitted. [https://www.news24.com/Africa/News/egypt-sentences-3-to-life-36-to-10-years-on-terror-charges-20180418 (News24)]
*[[Eternal derby of Bulgarian football]]
**A bomb explodes at a [[association football|football]] match between [[First Professional Football League (Bulgaria)|Bulgarian]] rivals [[PFC Levski Sofia|Levski Sofia]] and [[PFC CSKA Sofia|CSKA]] at the [[Vasil Levski National Stadium]] in [[Sofia]], injuring two police officers, one seriously. It is the second time a match between the two has seen an explosion, with a similar incident killing a man in 2000. [http://www.espn.co.uk/football/levski-sofia/story/3462993/sofia-derby-bomb-injures-policewoman-as-more-than-20-people-arrested (ESPN UK)]
*[[Reactions to the poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal]]
**[[United Kingdom|UK]] media regulator [[Ofcom]] launches investigations into [[RT (TV network)|RT]] over possible breaches of impartiality rules in its coverage of [[poisoning of Yulia and Sergei Skripal|the poisoning]]. Ofcom warns producer [[TV Novosti]] it may be forced to cease UK broadcasting. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-britain-russia/russias-rt-faces-seven-investigations-in-britain-over-broadcasts-since-skripal-case-idUKKBN1HP1CS (Reuters)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Cinema of Saudi Arabia]]
**A [[Censorship in Saudi Arabia|35-year ban on movie theaters ]] ends in [[Saudi Arabia]] with [[Marvel Studios]]' [[Black Panther (film)|''Black Panther'']] being the first film to show. [http://money.cnn.com/2018/04/18/media/saudi-arabia-movies-black-panther-amc/index.html (CNN)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economy of Iran]]
**[[Iran]]'s [[Central Bank of the Islamic Republic of Iran|central bank]] officially switches from using the [[United States dollar|U.S. dollar]] to the [[euro]] in its international transactions. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-currency-euro/iran-switches-from-dollar-to-euro-for-official-reporting-currency-idUSKBN1HP25W (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[list of shipwrecks in 2018|Shipwrecks in 2018]]
**[[Search and rescue]] operations end after a crewman missing after a fire broke out aboard drillship MV ''Geo Technical'' in the [[South China Sea]] yesterday is found dead on the vessel. A gas leak discovered today was hampering the efforts. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2018/04/18/gas-leak-makes-it-risky-to-search-for-missing-crewman-in-miri-ship-fire/ (''The Star'')] [https://www.maritime-executive.com/article/missing-crewmember-found-dead-aboard-burned-survey-vessel#gs.WH8lcww (The Maritime Executive)]
*[[2018 in Puerto Rico]]
**Puerto Rico experiences an island-wide [[Power outage|blackout]] after an excavator accidentally downs a transmission line. [https://apnews.com/f16313a8ccba490c94fd883e43db6bae (AP News)]
*[[List of accidents and incidents involving helicopters|Accidents involving helicopters]]
**An [[Iran]]ian helicopter crashes into the [[Persian Gulf]] whilst evacuating an unwell oil worker. Two people die. [https://en.trend.az/iran/2889210.html (Trend)]
*[[Associated Aviation Flight 361]]
**[[Nigeria]]n investigators release a final report finding the disaster occurred because of an unidentified engine malfunction which was mismanaged by the crew leading to a [[aerodynamic stall|stall]]. The resulting crash killed fifteen. [http://avherald.com/h?article=46961c3e/0003&opt=0 (The Aviation Herald)]
*[[Saratov Airlines Flight 703]]
**[[Russia]]n investigators say the flight crew received indications of a failure in the heating for the [[pitot-static system]], which measures parameters including airspeed. The crew received mismatching airspeed information prior to the crash near [[Moscow]]. All 71 on board died. [http://avherald.com/h?article=4b4cb236&opt=0 (The Aviation Herald)]
*A bus and a truck collide near [[Winterthur]], [[Switzerland]], injuring 15. [http://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/police-bus-crash-switzerland-leaves-15-hurt-54563881 (ABC News)]

;International relations
*[[Tajikistan–Uzbekistan relations]]
**[[Tajikistan]] and [[Uzbekistan]] agree to hold military drills for the first time. [https://en.trend.az/casia/uzbekistan/2889621.html (Trend)]
*[[Iran and weapons of mass destruction]]
**[[Iran]] reveals several new missiles on [[Islamic Republic of Iran Army Day]], including the new air missile defense system Kamin-2.  [https://www.tasnimnews.com/en/news/2018/04/18/1703318/iran-unveils-new-missile-system-in-parade (Tasmin News Agency)]

;Law and crime
*[[Criminal transmission of HIV#United Kingdom|Criminal transmission of HIV in the United Kingdom]]
**A [[Crown Court]] in [[England and Wales|England]] [[sentencing in England and Wales|jails]] Daryll Rowe for [[life imprisonment in England and Wales|life]] with a minimum of 12 years for deliberately infecting five men with [[HIV]] and attempting to infect five more. He is the first person convicted of deliberate HIV transmission in the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-sussex-43807662 (BBC News)]
*[[Basque conflict]]
**Basque separatist group [[Euskadi Ta Askatasuna|ETA]] announces its dissolution in May. [https://www.efe.com/efe/english/world/basque-separatist-group-eta-set-to-announce-dissolution-in-may/50000262-3589143 (EFE)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Cuban parliamentary election, 2018]]
**[[Cuba]]n president [[Raúl Castro]] prepares to step down as [[Miguel Díaz-Canel]] is elected as his successor.  This marks the first time since the [[Cuban Revolution]] that the country is not led by a member of the Castro family. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/amphtml/world/the_americas/in-cubas-national-assembly-raul-castro-marks-last-moments-of-his-familys-rule/2018/04/18/82f82cd4-4293-11e8-b2dc-b0a403e4720a_story.html (''Washington Post'')]
*[[Protests against Donald Trump]]
**[[Pittsburgh Police]] prepares large riot gears for a potential protest if [[Donald Trump]] fires [[Robert Mueller]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/morning-mix/wp/2018/04/19/pittsburgh-police-are-preparing-riot-gear-for-large-scale-protest-if-trump-fires-mueller/ (''Washington Post'')]
*[[2018 Nicaraguan protests|Protests in Nicaragua against Daniel Ortega]]
** Initially sparked by proposed social security reforms, culminated in demands for president [[Daniel Ortega]] to step down and a government crackdown. [https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2020/mar/11/over-100000-have-fled-nicaragua-since-brutal-2018-crackdown-says-un (''The Guardian'').]

;Science and technology
*[[2018 in spaceflight]]
**[[NASA]]'s [[Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite|TESS]] exoplanet [[space telescope]], whose launch was initially delayed, is successfully launched from [[Cape Canaveral Air Force Station]] by [[SpaceX]] on a [[Falcon 9]] rocket. The first stage of the rocket successfully landed on SpaceX's [[autonomous spaceport drone ship]] in the [[Atlantic Ocean]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/04/18/us/nasa-tess-satellite-launch/index.html (CNN)] [https://amp.space.com/40339-spacex-nasa-tess-launch-webcast.html (Space)]
*The [[U.S. Geological Survey]]'s [[Hawaiian Volcano Observatory]] states that [[Kīlauea]] is showing unusually high activity and that a new vent could form. [http://bigislandnow.com/2018/04/17/kilauea-volcano-showing-signs-of-increased-activity/ (Big Island Now)]
*[[Stratolaunch]] announce plans to test fly the world's largest plane this year. [https://www.engadget.com/2018/04/18/stratolaunch-first-flight-test/ (Engadget)]

;Sports

**Reports emerge [[Palestinian people|Palestinian]] cyclist Alaa Al-Daly, 21, had his leg amputated after being shot by an [[Israeli Defence Forces|Israeli sniper]] on the first day of the protests and as a result can no longer compete in the upcoming [[Asian Games]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-israeli-palestinians-protests-cyclist/wounded-gaza-cyclist-to-miss-asian-games-after-amputation-idUSKBN1HP2L3 (Reuters)]
